dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm that wording a never-verified (unbanked) placeholder as 'insufficient evidence, not a refutation' and stamping the insufficiency marker on it is intended, versus keeping unverified placeholders distinct from bounded-search insufficiency.
evidence: completion_verdict_assembly.py:95-104: unbanked branch sets `"unverified": True, "exhausted": True, "evidence_sufficient": False`
INSUFFICIENT_UNVERIFIED_DETAIL = 'criterion was never verified (recovery budget exhausted); insufficient evidence, not a refutation — recorded as an unverified placeholder.'

This treats 'never verified' identically to 'bounded search exhausted after looking', so the top-level insufficiency marker fires (and the honest-evidence remediation is chosen) even when nothing was ever searched for a criterion.
dropped.finding: The deterministic-assembly and merge unbanked placeholder (a criterion never verified at all) is now unconditionally stamped `evidence_sufficient: false` and worded as 'insufficient evidence, not a refutation'. A criterion that was never verified because the work is genuinely incomplete is now surfaced as an evidence-surfacing gap rather than an unverified/possibly-unmet criterion, softening the signal for genuinely-incomplete work.
scenarios: A recovery budget exhausts before any successor run reaches a criterion; the criterion becomes an unbanked placeholder marked insufficient, and reconcile_verdict may derive the top-level marker, presenting the FAIL as merely 'evidence insufficient' rather than 'unverified'.
